Good evening — I stood with working families to pass a bill that, quite simply, expands opportunity: we increased job‑training slots by 65% and boosted apprenticeship funding by 50%, creating real, local pathways into good‑paying careers; we did it by making big corporations finally pay more of their fair share so communities could invest in people, not handouts to special interests; the other side’s "wild exaggerations" ad is a desperate distraction from those concrete results, and I’m proud we delivered for families who need work, security, and a real chance to get ahead.  

When I speak with parents, teachers, and workers across our state I hear the same thing: people want action that opens doors to steady work and a future their kids can build on, and that’s exactly what this bill delivers — by expanding job‑training slots by 65% and increasing apprenticeship funding by roughly 50%, we put thousands more men and women into classrooms, into on‑the‑job training, and into direct hiring pipelines that lead to careers, not dead‑end gigs; those are not abstract numbers, they are people enrolling in training programs, apprentices clocking hours with local employers, and employers finally finding the skilled workers they need to grow — and we paid for that investment by closing favored loopholes and tightening rules so big corporations contribute more to the community investments they’ve long benefited from, allowing towns to fund new training centers, community colleges to scale up programs, and employers to partner on apprenticeships that lead to real jobs; opponents would rather headline a fact‑check about the scale than talk about the outcomes, so they run ads calling these gains "wild exaggerations," but voters see the new training classrooms, the apprentices showing up for work, and the employers hiring from local programs — that’s the record; if you want to argue about decimals, go ahead, but don’t ignore that we chose to invest in people and to require that corporations help pay for the infrastructure of a stronger workforce, and that choice is already delivering measurable results in neighborhoods across our state; at a time when too many politicians trade favors for headlines, we made a different choice — to stand with working families, expand opportunity at scale, and make powerful interests contribute to shared success — and I’ll keep fighting to make sure those gains reach every community that needs them.
